title: Verifying Thai ID Card Numbers: Genuine or Fake?

section1.heading: Did You Know?
section1.content: Did you know that we can manually verify a 13-digit National ID number to determine if it is a validly formatted ID or a fake one?

section2.heading: The 13 Digits are Divided into 5 Parts:
section2.content01: Part 1 (1st digit): Represents the category of the person holding the ID card. There are 8 categories in total.
section2.content02: Part 2 (Digits 2-5): Represents the registration office where the ID was issued. Digits 2-3 indicate the province, while digits 4-5 indicate the district, sub-district, or municipality.
section2.content03: Parts 3 and 4 (Digits 6-12): Represent the sequence of the person within their specific category and registration office.
section2.content04: Part 5 (13th digit): This is the 'Check Digit,' used to verify the mathematical accuracy of the entire 13-digit sequence.

section3.heading: The Check Digit
section3.content: Once we understand that the 13th digit is the validation key, we realize that this final number exists specifically to check the integrity of the 12 preceding digits.

section4.heading: Calculating the 13th Digit
section4.content: Since the 13th digit is a mathematical product of the first 12, we can calculate what that number *should* be. If our calculated value matches the 13th digit on the card, the ID number follows the official algorithm. If it doesn't match, the ID number is invalid.

section6.heading: How Secure is Our 13-Digit ID?
section6.content: That concludes our guide on verifying National ID numbers. Understanding the logic behind these digits is the first step in data validation. I hope this article is useful to everyone! Stay safe.
